label: def:information-speed-of-light
title: Speed of light as Lieb--Robinson velocity
html:
Definition. Speed of light as Lieb--Robinson velocity

Definition. The speed of light at substrate parameter q is the ratio of the spatial coupling weight q^{-1} to the temporal coupling weight \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} of the q-connection (q-connection):

  c_q  :=  \frac{q^{-1}}{\hbar_q}
  =  \frac{q^{-1}}{1 - q^{-1}}
  =  \frac{1}{q - 1}.

It is the ratio of spatial to temporal information transfer within a light cone (light cone) — a q-dependent quantity, not a postulated constant set to 1 by definition. Evaluated as the contact affine coordinate (contact affine chart) Z = \alpha_H / (\iota_\xi\alpha) on the q-connection, it measures the ratio of horizontal spatial diffusion to vertical quantum spin. This is the Lieb--Robinson velocity of the causal cone: the number of spatial information fibres correlated per unit of Reeb phase advance in one discrete f_q-iteration.
